Private Sub Form_QueryUnload(Cancel As Integer, UnloadMode As Integer)
    Dim iMSG As VbMsgBoxResult
    
    ' When a StoreFile is launched, we must quickly close up
    If GetLaunchingSTF = True Then
        Cancel = False
        Exit Sub
    End If
    
    ' A files is not being launched
    If GetFileFlag() = False Then
        iMSG = MsgBox("Are you sure you want to exit " & App.Title & "?", vbQuestion + vbYesNo)
        If iMSG = vbNo Then
            Cancel = True
        End If
        If iMSG = vbYes Then
            Cancel = False
        End If
    Else
        
        iMSG = MsgBox("Would you like to save your work before exiting?", vbQuestion + vbYesNoCancel, App.ProductName)
        If iMSG = vbYes Then
            ' File isn't saved yet.  Show a Save As dialog
            If LCase$(GetFileName()) = "untitled" Then
                Dim strSaveFile As String
                strSaveFile = DisplaySaveAs()
                If strSaveFile = "32755" Then
                    ' User clicked Cancel in the Save As dialog
                    Cancel = True
                    Exit Sub
                End If
                
                ' Write that filename to memory
                SetFileName (strSaveFile)
            End If
            
            ' Write data to disk
            SaveStoreFile Me, GetFileName()
            Cancel = False
        End If
        If iMSG = vbNo Then
            Cancel = False
        End If
        If iMSG = vbCancel Then
            ' Cancel.  No exit, No save.
            Cancel = True
        End If
    End If
End Sub

Attribute VB_Name = "TStoreMod"
Option Explicit



' On Windows XP or later, turns on Visual Styles
Public Declare Function InitCommonControls Lib "comctl32.dll" () As Long

'Allows us to have a return code (use in place of an End statement)
Public Declare Sub ExitProcess Lib "kernel32" (ByVal uExitCode As Long)

Sub Main()
    ' Checks the command line to see if we have a file to operate on
    ' /e filename.stf to Edit a file
    ' /l filename.stf to Launch a file
    Dim intCmdReturn As Integer
    intCmdReturn = CheckCommandLine(Command$)
    
    ' Tells StoreTrainer that we want to turn on Visual Styles in Windows XP or later
    InitCommonControls
    
    ' Let's create TStore.INI if necessary
    If GetStoreTrainerDataFile = "" Then
        CreateStoreTrainerData
    End If
    
    ' Let's refresh the StoreTrainer Path if necessary
    ' This is primarily used for refreshing when switching from DEBUG to PRODUCTION
    Dim strCurPath As String
    strCurPath = IniGetValueString(GetStoreTrainerDataFile, "General", "Path", "PATH_NAME")
    If strCurPath <> App.Path Then
        Dim iMSG As VbMsgBoxResult
        iMSG = MsgBox("The " & App.ProductName & " configuration settings need to be updated.  Do that now?", vbYesNoCancel + vbQuestion, App.ProductName)
        If iMSG = vbCancel Then ExitProcess 4 'User Canceled updating TSTORE.INI
        If iMSG = vbYes Then
            IniWriteValueString GetStoreTrainerDataFile, "General", "Path", App.Path
        End If
    End If
        

    ' Let's make sure the StoreFile folder exists
    ' By default, it should be <MY_DOCUMENTS>\StoreFiles
    Dim strSTFFolder As String
    strSTFFolder = GetStoreFileFolder(True, True)
    If (strSTFFolder = "NO_FOLDER_CREATED") Then
        ' Error: folder does not exist, or wasn't created
        MsgBox App.ProductName & " requires that you create a StoreFile folder.  Now exiting!", vbCritical, App.ProductName
        
        ' Exit with a Code 1 ERROR_NO_STF_FOLDER
        ExitProcess 1
    End If
    ' Brings up the main screen
    frmMain.Show
End Sub

' This checks for a command line switch being passed in
' Returns an integer based on results:
' 0 - no command line switch found, load as normal
' 1 - File loaded for editing /e filename.stf
' 2 - File loaded for launching /l filename.stf
Public Function CheckCommandLine(Optional CommandLine As String = "") As Integer
    
End Function

Public Sub AboutStoreTrainer()
    MsgBox App.ProductName & " v" & App.Major & "." & App.Minor & "." & App.Revision & vbCrLf & "" & vbCrLf & "Copyright (C) 2024-2025 " & App.CompanyName, vbInformation + vbOKOnly, App.ProductName
End Sub

Public Sub CreateStoreTrainerData()
    ' First, let's create folders as necessary
    Dim FSO As FileSystemObject
    Set FSO = CreateObject("Scripting.FileSystemObject")
    If Not FSO.FolderExists(FGetSpecialFolder(CSIDL_APPDATA) & "\RaggieSoft") Then
        MkDir FGetSpecialFolder(CSIDL_APPDATA) & "\RaggieSoft"
    End If
    If Not FSO.FolderExists(FGetSpecialFolder(CSIDL_APPDATA) & "\RaggieSoft\StoreTrainer") Then
        MkDir FGetSpecialFolder(CSIDL_APPDATA) & "\RaggieSoft\StoreTrainer"
    End If
    
    ' Now, let's work on StoreTrainer data
    IniWriteValueString GetStoreTrainerDataDir & "\TStore.ini", "General", "Version", App.Major & "." & App.Minor & "." & App.Revision
    IniWriteValueString GetStoreTrainerDataDir & "\TStore.ini", "General", "Path", App.Path
End Sub

Public Function GetStoreTrainerDataDir() As String
    GetStoreTrainerDataDir = FGetSpecialFolder(CSIDL_APPDATA) & "\RaggieSoft\StoreTrainer"
End Function
Public Function GetStoreTrainerDataFile() As String
    If DoesFileExist(FGetSpecialFolder(CSIDL_APPDATA) & "\RaggieSoft\StoreTrainer\TStore.ini") Then
        GetStoreTrainerDataFile = FGetSpecialFolder(CSIDL_APPDATA) & "\RaggieSoft\StoreTrainer\TStore.ini"
    Else
        GetStoreTrainerDataFile = ""
    End If
End Function

    Dim strSTFVersion As String

    Dim iSTFCompare As Integer

    If iSTFCompare = 1 Then
        OpenStoreFile = 1
        Exit Function
    End If

Public Function GetFileName(Optional showFileNameOnly As Boolean) As String

    strLocalFileName = strFileName
    Dim boolHideExtensions As Boolean
    If showFileNameOnly = True Then
        ' Needed if the user wants to only show the filename without path
        Dim FSO As FileSystemObject
        Set FSO = CreateObject("Scripting.FileSystemObject")
        ' Return the filename without a path
        ' First, we see if the user wants file extensions hidden or not (it's a user setting in Windows Explorer)
        ' Apparently this is hardened in Vista+ (see cantReadRegistry below)
        boolHideExtensions = CBool(RegGetValue$(HKEY_CURRENT_USER, "Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Advanced", "HideFileExt"))
        If boolHideExtensions Then
            strLocalFileName = FSO.GetBaseName(strLocalFileName)
        Else
            strLocalFileName = FSO.GetFileName(strLocalFileName)
        End If
        
        ' Return that to the user
        GetFileName = strLocalFileName
        Exit Function
    End If
    ' Return the full filename
    GetFileName = strFileName
    Exit Function
cantReadRegistry:
    ' assume we don't have access to the Registry, we will NOT hide the extensions
    ' Seems to be an issue with newer versions of Windows (because VB6 doesn't understand Registry Security)
    boolHideExtensions = False
    Resume Next

Public Function Launch() As Integer
    ' Let's launch our StoreFile.  RULES:
    ' * File must NOT be dirty
    ' * Game and Trainer path MUST exist (unless of course, the trainer launches the game)
    ' * Returns an integer based on error type.  Anything non-zero means error
    
    ' Set up the FileSystem object
    Dim FSO As FileSystemObject
    Set FSO = CreateObject("Scripting.FileSystemObject")
    
    ' Is the file dirty?
    If GetFileFlag = True Or GetFileName = "untitled" Then
        Launch = 1 ' File isn't saved.  Return code 1
        Exit Function
    End If
    
    ' Look for the trainer
    If DoesFileExist(GetTrainerPath) = False Then
        Launch = 2 ' Trainer doesn't exist.  Return code 2
        Exit Function
    End If
    
    ' Look for the game (if it's NOT launched by the trainer)
    If GetTrainerLaunchesGame = False Then
        If DoesFileExist(GetGamePath) = False Then
            Launch = 3 ' Game doesn't exist.  Return code 3
            Exit Function
        End If
    End If
    
    ' Checked all our errors.  Let's launch files
    ' Let's build our file paths
    Dim strGameAndSwitch As String, strTrainerAndSwitch As String
    strGameAndSwitch = Chr$(34) & GetGamePath & Chr$(34)
    If GetGameSwitch <> "" Then
        strGameAndSwitch = strGameAndSwitch & " " & Chr$(34) & GetGameSwitch & Chr$(34)
    End If
    strTrainerAndSwitch = Chr$(34) & GetTrainerPath & Chr$(34)
    If GetTrainerSwitch <> "" Then
        strTrainerAndSwitch = strTrainerAndSwitch & " " & Chr$(34) & GetTrainerSwitch & Chr$(34)
    End If
    
    ' We are ready to launch.  Don't forget to get the ParentFolder property because some trainers (and games?) expect the working folder to be set
    
    ' Now to see what to launch
    If GetLaunchGameFirst = True Then
        
        ' Fall back, just in case
        If GetTrainerLaunchesGame = False Then
            ChDrive GetGamePath()
            ChDir GetGamePath()
            Shell strGameAndSwitch, vbNormalFocus
            DoEvents
        End If
        ChDrive GetTrainerPath()
        ChDir GetTrainerPath()
        Shell strTrainerAndSwitch, vbNormalFocus
        DoEvents
        Launch = 0
        Exit Function
    End If
    
    ' We just need to launch the trainer
    If GetTrainerLaunchesGame = True Then
        ChDrive GetTrainerPath()
        ChDir GetTrainerPath()
        Shell strTrainerAndSwitch, vbNormalFocus
        Launch = 0
        Exit Function
    End If
    
    ' None of the options are selected.  Launch both
    ChDrive GetGamePath()
    ChDir GetGamePath()
    Shell strGameAndSwitch, vbNormalFocus
    DoEvents
    ChDrive GetTrainerPath()
    ChDir GetTrainerPath()
    Shell strTrainerAndSwitch, vbNormalFocus
    DoEvents
    Launch = 0
    Exit Function
    
End Function

Attribute VB_Name = "OSVersionInfo"
Option Explicit
' NOTE: in order for calls to GetVersionEx to function properly,
' you must include a manifest file with correct supportedOS entries
'
' Otherwise, calls will always return 6.2 at most on VER_PLATFORM_WIN32_NT

Private Declare Function GetVersionEx Lib "kernel32" Alias "GetVersionExA" _
    (lpVersionInformation As OSVERSIONINFO) As Long

Private Type OSVERSIONINFO
  OSVSize         As Long
  dwVerMajor      As Long
  dwVerMinor      As Long
  dwBuildNumber   As Long
  PlatformID      As Long
  szCSDVersion    As String * 128
End Type

Public Enum osArch
    VER_PLATFORM_WIN32s = 0 'Windows 3.x with Win32s Library
    VER_PLATFORM_WIN32_WINDOWS = 1 'Windows 9x
    VER_PLATFORM_WIN32_NT = 2 'Windows NT
End Enum
' Let's provide a public way to access Version Information
Public Type osInfo
    osArchitecture As osArch
    osVersionMajor As Long
    osVersionMinor As Long
    osVersionBuild As Long
    osServicePack As Long
End Type

Public Function GetWinVer() As osInfo
    Dim osv As OSVERSIONINFO
    osv.OSVSize = Len(osv)
    If GetVersionEx(osv) = 1 Then
        GetWinVer.osVersionMajor = osv.dwVerMajor
        GetWinVer.osVersionMinor = osv.dwVerMinor
        GetWinVer.osVersionBuild = osv.dwBuildNumber
        GetWinVer.osServicePack = -1 'Trap for no service pack (Windows 9x?)
        Select Case osv.PlatformID
            Case VER_PLATFORM_WIN32s
                GetWinVer.osArchitecture = VER_PLATFORM_WIN32s
            Case VER_PLATFORM_WIN32_NT
                GetWinVer.osArchitecture = VER_PLATFORM_WIN32_NT
                
                ' Service Pack
                
                
                
                ' It's a pain in the rear to strip the number from the string, but here goes
                ' We're going from a String() - a Character Array - to a String to a Long
                Dim pos As Integer
                pos = InStr(osv.szCSDVersion, Chr$(0)) 'Get the string "Service Pack #" as an Array
                If pos Then
                    On Error GoTo NoSP 'Handle not having a Service Pack
                    Dim sSPName As String
                    sSPName = Left$(osv.szCSDVersion, pos - 1) 'Convert from a String() to a String
                    sSPName = Right$(sSPName, 1) 'Strip the Service Pack number from the string
                    Dim lSPNum As Long
                    lSPNum = CLng(sSPName) 'Convert the service pack number from a String to a Long
                    GetWinVer.osServicePack = lSPNum 'Offer it to the user
                    GoTo FinishNT 'We're done, if a Service Pack is installed
NoSP:
                    GetWinVer.osServicePack = 0 'No Service Pack installed (or we couldn't parse the Service Pack information)
                End If
FinishNT:
            Case VER_PLATFORM_WIN32_WINDOWS:
                GetWinVer.osArchitecture = VER_PLATFORM_WIN32_WINDOWS
        End Select

    End If

End Function

' Returns the version of Windows that the user is running
Public Function GetWindowsVersion() As String
    Dim osv As OSVERSIONINFO
    osv.OSVSize = Len(osv)

    If GetVersionEx(osv) = 1 Then
        Select Case osv.PlatformID
            Case VER_PLATFORM_WIN32s
                GetWindowsVersion = "Win32s on Windows 3.1"
            Case VER_PLATFORM_WIN32_NT
                GetWindowsVersion = "Windows NT"

                Select Case osv.dwVerMajor
                    Case 3
                        GetWindowsVersion = "Windows NT 3.5"
                    Case 4
                        GetWindowsVersion = "Windows NT 4.0"
                    Case 5
                        Select Case osv.dwVerMinor
                            Case 0
                                GetWindowsVersion = "Windows 2000"
                            Case 1
                                GetWindowsVersion = "Windows XP"
                            Case 2
                                GetWindowsVersion = "Windows Server 2003"
                        End Select
                    Case 6
                        Select Case osv.dwVerMinor
                            Case 0
                                GetWindowsVersion = "Windows Vista/Server 2008"
                            Case 1
                                GetWindowsVersion = "Windows 7/Server 2008 R2"
                            Case 2
                                GetWindowsVersion = "Windows 8/Server 2012"
                            Case 3
                                GetWindowsVersion = "Windows 8.1/Server 2012 R2"
                        End Select
                    Case 10
                        GetWindowsVersion = "Windows 10"

    Dim handle As Long

    is64Bit = False

Attribute VB_Name = "VersionCompare"
Option Explicit
Public Function CompareFileVersion(sFileName1 As String, sFileName2 As String) As Integer

    '// Return values:
    '// -1 = File Version 2 is greater than File Version 1
    '//  0 = Versions are the same
    '//  1 = File version 1 is greater than File Version 2
    Dim iResult As Integer

    Dim sFileVersion1 As String
    Dim sFileVersion2 As String
    Dim arrFileVersion1() As String
    Dim arrFileVersion2() As String
    Dim lVersion1 As Long
    Dim lVersion2 As Long
    Dim fs As FileSystemObject

    '// Let's initialize our result with 0
    iResult = 0

    '// Use FileSystemObject to get the file version
    Set fs = CreateObject("Scripting.FileSystemObject")
    sFileVersion1 = fs.GetFileVersion(sFileName1)
    sFileVersion2 = fs.GetFileVersion(sFileName2)

    '// Split the two supplied file versions by the "." character
    arrFileVersion1() = Split(sFileVersion1, ".")
    arrFileVersion2() = Split(sFileVersion2, ".")
    
    Dim i As Integer
    For i = 0 To UBound(arrFileVersion1())
        '// Convert the string to a number so we don't get false positive ("2">"19")
        lVersion1 = CLng(arrFileVersion1(i))
        lVersion2 = CLng(arrFileVersion2(i))
        If lVersion1 > lVersion2 Then
            iResult = 1
        ElseIf lVersion1 < lVersion2 Then
            iResult = -1
        End If

        'If we have found that the result is not > or <, no need to proceed
        If iResult <> 0 Then Exit For

    Next

    If UBound(arrFileVersion2) > UBound(arrFileVersion1) _
      And arrFileVersion2(UBound(arrFileVersion2)) <> 0 Then iResult = -1

    CompareFileVersion = iResult

End Function

Public Function CheckVersion(ByVal par1 As String, ByVal par2 As String) As Integer
    Dim arr1() As String
    Dim arr2() As String
    Dim looper As Integer
    Dim returnValue As Integer
    Dim val1 As Integer
    Dim val2 As Integer
    arr1 = Split(par1, ".")
    arr2 = Split(par2, ".")

    For looper = 0 To Max(UBound(arr1), UBound(arr2))
        val1 = 0
        val2 = 0
        If UBound(arr1) >= looper Then
            val1 = Val(arr1(looper))
        End If
        If UBound(arr2) >= looper Then
            val2 = Val(arr2(looper))
        End If

        If val1 > val2 Then
            returnValue = 1
            Exit For
        ElseIf val1 < val2 Then
            returnValue = -1
            Exit For
        Else
            ' same #, keep going
        End If
    Next
    CheckVersion = returnValue
End Function

Public Function Max(ByVal par1 As Integer, ByVal par2 As Integer) As Integer
    If par1 > par2 Then
        Max = par1
    Else
        Max = par2
    End If
End Function

-----------------------

StoreTrainer is an easy way to remember the location of games and trainers (the common name for cheat programs). 	'UPGRADE_WARNING: Form event frmMain.QueryUnload has a new behavior. Click for more: 'ms-help://MS.VSCC.2003/commoner/redir/redirect.htm?keyword="vbup2065"'
	Private Sub frmMain_Closing(ByVal eventSender As System.Object, ByVal eventArgs As System.ComponentModel.CancelEventArgs) Handles MyBase.Closing
		Dim Cancel As Short = eventArgs.Cancel
		Dim iMSG As MsgBoxResult
		
		' When a StoreFile is launched, we must quickly close up
		If GetLaunchingSTF = True Then
			Cancel = False
			GoTo EventExitSub
		End If
		
		' A files is not being launched
		Dim strSaveFile As String
		If GetFileFlag() = False Then
			iMSG = MsgBox("Are you sure you want to exit " & System.Reflection.Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly.GetName.Name & "?", MsgBoxStyle.Question + MsgBoxStyle.YesNo)
			If iMSG = MsgBoxResult.No Then
				Cancel = True
			End If
			If iMSG = MsgBoxResult.Yes Then
				Cancel = False
			End If
		Else
			
			iMSG = MsgBox("Would you like to save your work before exiting?", MsgBoxStyle.Question + MsgBoxStyle.YesNoCancel, System.Diagnostics.FileVersionInfo.GetVersionInfo(System.Reflection.Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly.Location).ProductName)
			If iMSG = MsgBoxResult.Yes Then
				' File isn't saved yet.  Show a Save As dialog
				If LCase(GetFileName()) = "untitled" Then
					strSaveFile = DisplaySaveAs()
					If strSaveFile = "32755" Then
						' User clicked Cancel in the Save As dialog
						Cancel = True
						GoTo EventExitSub
					End If
					
					' Write that filename to memory
					SetFileName((strSaveFile))
				End If
				
				' Write data to disk
				SaveStoreFile(Me, GetFileName())
				Cancel = False
			End If
			If iMSG = MsgBoxResult.No Then
				Cancel = False
			End If
			If iMSG = MsgBoxResult.Cancel Then
				' Cancel.  No exit, No save.
				Cancel = True
			End If
		End If
EventExitSub: 
		eventArgs.Cancel = Cancel
	End Sub

			DisplaySaveAs = "32755"
			Exit Function
		End If

	' Tells StoreTrainer if the file is saved or not
	Public Sub SetFileFlag(ByRef dirtyFlag As Boolean, ByRef frmName As System.Windows.Forms.Form)
		On Error GoTo ErrorTrap
		Dim errorType As String
		errorType = "Not Yet Set"
		If dirtyFlag = True Then
			errorType = "Dirty = true"
			isFileDirty = True
			frmName.Text = GetFileName(True) & " * - " & System.Diagnostics.FileVersionInfo.GetVersionInfo(System.Reflection.Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly.Location).ProductName
		ElseIf dirtyFlag = False Then 
			errorType = "Dirty = false"
			isFileDirty = False
			errorType = errorType & " - Did Set Flag"
			frmName.Text = GetFileName(True) & " - " & System.Diagnostics.FileVersionInfo.GetVersionInfo(System.Reflection.Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly.Location).ProductName
			errorType = errorType & " - Did (not) Set Form Name"
		Else
			MsgBox("Improper Usage: setFileFlag() requires true or false!", MsgBoxStyle.Exclamation + MsgBoxStyle.OKOnly, System.Diagnostics.FileVersionInfo.GetVersionInfo(System.Reflection.Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly.Location).ProductName)

	' This writes StoreFile data to disk
	Public Function SaveStoreFile(ByRef frmName As System.Windows.Forms.Form, ByRef strFileName As String) As Short
		On Error GoTo ErrorTrapper
		' Write StoreFile data to the disk
		
		' General Info
		IniWriteValueString(strFileName, "General", "STF.Version", GetSTFVersionStr)
		
		
		' Trainer Launches Game
		Dim strTrainerLaunchesGame As String
		If GetTrainerLaunchesGame() = True Then
			strTrainerLaunchesGame = "true"
		End If
		If GetTrainerLaunchesGame() = False Then
			strTrainerLaunchesGame = "false"
		End If
		IniWriteValueString(strFileName, "Trainer", "TrainerLaunchesGame", strTrainerLaunchesGame)
		
		' Launch Game First
		Dim strLaunchGameFirst As String
		If GetLaunchGameFirst() = True Then
			strLaunchGameFirst = "true"
		End If
		If GetLaunchGameFirst() = False Then
			strLaunchGameFirst = "false"
		End If
		IniWriteValueString(strFileName, "Game", "LaunchGameFirst", strLaunchGameFirst)
		
		' Write Game and Trainer info
		IniWriteValueString(strFileName, "Game", "Path", GetGamePath)
		IniWriteValueString(strFileName, "Game", "Switch", GetGameSwitch)
		
		IniWriteValueString(strFileName, "Trainer", "Path", GetTrainerPath)
		IniWriteValueString(strFileName, "Trainer", "Switch", GetTrainerSwitch)
		
		' Unset the Dirty flag
		SetFileFlag(False, frmName)
		
		' Reports no error on saving
		SaveStoreFile = 0
		Exit Function
		
		' Error Trapping
ErrorTrapper: '
		
		SaveStoreFile = Err.Number
	End Function
	
	' Opens a StoreFile.  NOTE: this does NOT fill in the textboxes on a form
	' Any return non-zero is an error
	Public Function OpenStoreFile(ByRef strFilePath As String) As Short
		Dim FSO As IWshRuntimeLibrary.FileSystemObject
		FSO = CreateObject("Scripting.FileSystemObject")
		
		'Let's see if the file exists or not (return 53 (the same as VB6's File Not Found error) if it doesn't)
		If Not FSO.FileExists(strFilePath) Then
			OpenStoreFile = 53
			Exit Function
		End If
		
		' File does exist.  Let's make sure it's a StoreFile this version of StoreTrainer understands
		Dim strSTFVersion As String
		strSTFVersion = IniGetValueString(strFilePath, "General", "STF.Version", "0.0")
		Dim iSTFCompare As Short
		iSTFCompare = CheckVersion(strSTFVersion, GetSTFVersionStr)
		
		' The file being opened expects a newer version of StoreTrainer
		If iSTFCompare = 1 Then
			OpenStoreFile = 1
			Exit Function
		End If
		
		' The file being opened expects an older version of StoreTrainer
		If iSTFCompare = -1 Then
			OpenStoreFile = 2
			Exit Function
		End If
		
		' Now, let's load data into memory
		' THIS WILL NOT LOAD DATA INTO A FORM
		
		' Load Launch Data
		Dim strTrainerLaunchesGame As String
		strTrainerLaunchesGame = IniGetValueString(strFilePath, "Trainer", "TrainerLaunchesGame", "false")
		
		If strTrainerLaunchesGame = "true" Then
			SetTrainerLaunchesGame(True)
		Else
			SetTrainerLaunchesGame(False)
		End If
		
		Dim strLaunchGameFirst As String
		strLaunchGameFirst = IniGetValueString(strFilePath, "Game", "LaunchGameFirst", "false")
		If strLaunchGameFirst = "true" Then
			SetLaunchGameFirst(True)
		Else
			SetLaunchGameFirst(False)
		End If
		
		' Get the Game and Trainer path and switches
		SetGamePath(IniGetValueString(strFilePath, "Game", "Path", vbNullString))
		SetGameSwitch(IniGetValueString(strFilePath, "Game", "Switch", vbNullString))
		
		SetTrainerPath(IniGetValueString(strFilePath, "Trainer", "Path", vbNullString))
		SetTrainerSwitch(IniGetValueString(strFilePath, "Trainer", "Switch", vbNullString))
		
		' We're done. It is up to you to populate the form
		OpenStoreFile = 0
	End Function
	
	Public Sub SetFileName(ByRef strLocalFileName As String)
		strFileName = strLocalFileName
	End Sub
	
	Public Function GetFileName(Optional ByRef showFileNameOnly As Boolean = False) As String
		On Error GoTo cantReadRegistry
		' Pull the filename from memory
		Dim strLocalFileName As String
		strLocalFileName = strFileName
		Dim boolHideExtensions As Boolean
		Dim FSO As IWshRuntimeLibrary.FileSystemObject
		If showFileNameOnly = True Then
			' Needed if the user wants to only show the filename without path
			FSO = CreateObject("Scripting.FileSystemObject")
			' Return the filename without a path
			' First, we see if the user wants file extensions hidden or not (it's a user setting in Windows Explorer)
			' Apparently this is hardened in Vista+ (see cantReadRegistry below)
			boolHideExtensions = CBool(RegGetValue(HKEY_CURRENT_USER, "Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Advanced", "HideFileExt"))
			If boolHideExtensions Then
				strLocalFileName = FSO.GetBaseName(strLocalFileName)
			Else
				strLocalFileName = FSO.GetFileName(strLocalFileName)
			End If
			
			' Return that to the user
			GetFileName = strLocalFileName
			Exit Function
		End If
		' Return the full filename
		GetFileName = strFileName
		Exit Function
cantReadRegistry: 
		' assume we don't have access to the Registry, we will NOT hide the extensions
		' Seems to be an issue with newer versions of Windows (because VB6 doesn't understand Registry Security)
		boolHideExtensions = False
		Resume Next
	End Function
	
	Public Function Launch() As Short
		' Let's launch our StoreFile.  RULES:
		' * File must NOT be dirty
		' * Game and Trainer path MUST exist (unless of course, the trainer launches the game)
		' * Returns an integer based on error type.  Anything non-zero means error
		
		' Set up the FileSystem object
		Dim FSO As IWshRuntimeLibrary.FileSystemObject
		FSO = CreateObject("Scripting.FileSystemObject")
		
		' Is the file dirty?
		If GetFileFlag = True Or GetFileName = "untitled" Then
			Launch = 1 ' File isn't saved.  Return code 1
			Exit Function
		End If
		
		' Look for the trainer
		If DoesFileExist(GetTrainerPath) = False Then
			Launch = 2 ' Trainer doesn't exist.  Return code 2
			Exit Function
		End If
		
		' Look for the game (if it's NOT launched by the trainer)
		If GetTrainerLaunchesGame = False Then
			If DoesFileExist(GetGamePath) = False Then
				Launch = 3 ' Game doesn't exist.  Return code 3
				Exit Function
			End If
		End If
		
		' Checked all our errors.  Let's launch files
		' Let's build our file paths
		Dim strGameAndSwitch, strTrainerAndSwitch As String
		strGameAndSwitch = Chr(34) & GetGamePath & Chr(34)
		If GetGameSwitch <> "" Then
			strGameAndSwitch = strGameAndSwitch & " " & Chr(34) & GetGameSwitch & Chr(34)
		End If
		strTrainerAndSwitch = Chr(34) & GetTrainerPath & Chr(34)
		If GetTrainerSwitch <> "" Then
			strTrainerAndSwitch = strTrainerAndSwitch & " " & Chr(34) & GetTrainerSwitch & Chr(34)
		End If
		
		' We are ready to launch.  Don't forget to get the ParentFolder property because some trainers (and games?) expect the working folder to be set
		
		' Now to see what to launch
		If GetLaunchGameFirst = True Then
			
			' Fall back, just in case
			If GetTrainerLaunchesGame = False Then
				ChDrive(GetGamePath())
				ChDir(GetGamePath())
				Shell(strGameAndSwitch, AppWinStyle.NormalFocus)
				System.Windows.Forms.Application.DoEvents()
			End If
			ChDrive(GetTrainerPath())
			ChDir(GetTrainerPath())
			Shell(strTrainerAndSwitch, AppWinStyle.NormalFocus)
			System.Windows.Forms.Application.DoEvents()
			Launch = 0
			Exit Function
		End If
		
		' We just need to launch the trainer
		If GetTrainerLaunchesGame = True Then
			ChDrive(GetTrainerPath())
			ChDir(GetTrainerPath())
			Shell(strTrainerAndSwitch, AppWinStyle.NormalFocus)
			Launch = 0
			Exit Function
		End If
		
		' None of the options are selected.  Launch both
		ChDrive(GetGamePath())
		ChDir(GetGamePath())
		Shell(strGameAndSwitch, AppWinStyle.NormalFocus)
		System.Windows.Forms.Application.DoEvents()
		ChDrive(GetTrainerPath())
		ChDir(GetTrainerPath())
		Shell(strTrainerAndSwitch, AppWinStyle.NormalFocus)
		System.Windows.Forms.Application.DoEvents()
		Launch = 0
		Exit Function
		
	End Function
End Module

	!insertmacro MUI_DESCRIPTION_TEXT ${Src} $(DESC_Src)

;This runs when the program is uninstalling
Section "Uninstall"
	;We want Shortcuts to be for All Users
	SetShellVarContext all
	
	;Grab the proper installation folder (in case the uninstaller is in the wrong place)
	ReadRegStr $INSTDIR HKLM "Software\$CompanyName\$ProductName" "Installation Folder"
	
	;Remove our Registry keys
	DetailPrint "Deleting Registry Keys"
	DeleteRegKey HKLM "Software\Microsoft Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\$CompanyName $ProductName"
	DeleteRegKey HKLM "Software\$CompanyName\$ProductName"
	DeleteRegKey /ifempty HKLM "Software\$CompanyName"
	
	;Remove $ProductName's executable
	DetailPrint "Uninstalling $ProductName"
	RMDir /r /REBOOTOK "$INSTDIR\Source" ;Recursively search the folder to clear out any extra files
	Delete "$INSTDIR\TStore.exe"
	Delete "$INSTDIR\TStore.exe.manifest"
	Delete "$INSTDIR\License.rtf"
	Delete "$INSTDIR\README.txt"
	Delete "$INSTDIR\TStore.ini"
	Delete "$INSTDIR\uninstall.exe"
	RMDir "$INSTDIR" ;DO NOT do a /r recursive search (in case, for example, someone installed to C:\Program Files this would really mess up the users computer)
	RMDir $PROGRAMFILES\$CompanyName ;AGAIN, do NOT use /r (this deletes it ONLY IF EMPTY)
	
	DetailPrint "Deleting Shortcuts"
	Delete "$SMPROGRAMS\$ProductName.lnk"
	
	;We are DONE with uninstall
	;As a reminder, DO NOT TOUCH any of the Microsoft DLLs that get installed
	;Also, $ProductName's per-user files do not get uninstalled (it's just not possible to remove files for users other than your own in the main uninstaller, however it is possible to release a utility that does PER-USER cleaning)
	
SectionEnd

;We need to do some checks when the installer and uninstaller are started.

;Tests for Admin rights NT4/2000/XP
;Also works if somehow UAC is disabled or broken on Vista+
;Also, on Windows NT 4.0, the Visual Basic runtime requires Service Pack 3 or later installed
Function .onInit
	;Company and Product
	StrCpy $CompanyName "RaggieSoft"
	StrCpy $ProductName "StoreTrainer"
	
	;Redefine the install folder
	StrCpy $INSTDIR "$PROGRAMFILES\$CompanyName\$ProductName"
	
	;Check for NT Admin Rights
	UserInfo::GetAccountType
	pop $0
	${If} $0 != "admin" ;Require admin rights on NT4+
		MessageBox MB_ICONSTOP|MB_OK "Administrator rights required to install $ProductName!" /SD IDOK
		SetErrorLevel 740 ;ERROR_ELEVATION_REQUIRED
		Quit
	${EndIf}

	;Check for NT 4.0 SP3 or higher
	;Otherwise, $ProductName *SHOULD* be able to run on any other 32bit or 64bit OS
	;That is Windows 95 or later.  Sorry Windows 3.1
	${If} ${IsNT}
		${If} ${IsWinNT4}
			${If} ${AtMostServicePack} 2
				MessageBox MB_ICONSTOP|MB_OK "Service Pack 3 or higher is required for Windows NT 4.0" /SD IDOK
				SetErrorLevel 3 ;3 because Service Pack 3 (pun intended)
				Quit
			${EndIf}
		${EndIf}
	${EndIf}
	
	;Detect previous version
	ReadRegStr  $IS_INSTALLED HKLM "Software\$CompanyName\$ProductName" "Installation Folder"
	IfFileExists "$IS_INSTALLED\uninstall.exe" FileFound EndFileExistsTest
	FileFound:
		;Let's check file versions.
		${GetFileVersion} "$INSTDIR\TStore.exe" $R0
		${GetFileVersion} "$EXEPATH" $R1
		${VersionCompare} $R0 $R1 $TSTORESETUP
		
		;This installer is the same as what is already installed
		${If} $TSTORESETUP == 0
			Exec "$IS_INSTALLED\uninstall.exe"
			SetErrorLevel 4
			Quit
		${EndIf}
		
		;This installer has an older version of $ProductName
		${If} $TSSETUP == 1
			MessageBox MB_ICONSTOP|MB_OK "This installer contains an older version of $ProductName.$\r$\nSetup will now close." /SD IDOK
			SetErrorLevel 5
			Quit
		${EndIf}
	EndFileExistsTest:

		
FunctionEnd
Function un.onInit
	;Company and Product
	StrCpy $CompanyName "RaggieSoft"
	StrCpy $ProductName "StoreTrainer"
	
	UserInfo::GetAccountType
	pop $0
	${If} $0 != "admin" ;Require admin rights on NT4+
		MessageBox MB_ICONSTOP|MB_OK "Administrator rights required to uninstall $ProductName!" /SD IDOK
		SetErrorLevel 740 ;ERROR_ELEVATION_REQUIRED
		Quit
	${EndIf}
FunctionEnd

; $ProductName Install
Section "$CompanyName $ProductName" TStoreBase
	; Install Files
	SetOutPath $INSTDIR
	SetOverwrite ifnewer
	DetailPrint "Installing $ProductName"
	File "..\Build\TStore.exe"
	File "..\Build\TStore.exe.manifest"
	File "..\README.txt"
	File "License\LICENSE.rtf"
	
	; Create master TSTORE.INI file (meant to be read-only)
	Var /GLOBAL TSTOREVER
	${GetFileVersion} "$INSTDIR\TStore.exe" $TSTOREVER
	WriteINIStr "$INSTDIR\TStore.ini" "General" "Version" "$TSTOREVER"
	WriteINIStr "$INSTDIR\TStore.ini" "General" "Path" "$INSTDIR"
	
	; Create Shortcut
	CreateShortcut "$SMPROGRAMS\$ProductName.lnk" "$INSTDIR\TStore.exe" "" "$INSTDIR\TStore.exe" 0 SW_SHOWNORMAL "" "$ProductName stores the locations of your games and trainers in an easy to use format"
	
	; Create $ProductName Registry entries
	WriteRegStr HKLM "Software\$CompanyName\$ProductName" "Installation Folder" "$INSTDIR"
	WriteRegStr HKLM "Software\$CompanyName\$ProductName" "Product Version" "$TSTOREVER"
	WriteRegStr HKLM "Software\$CompanyName\$ProductName" "SMFolder" "$SMPROGRAMS"
	WriteRegStr HKLM "Software\$CompanyName\$ProductName" "Uninstall Key Location" "Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\$CompanyName $ProductName"
	
SectionEnd

Section "-Unistall Registry Keys" Unins
	; Create Uninstall Registry Entries
	DetailPrint "Creating Uninstaller"
	Var /GLOBAL UNINSREG
	StrCpy $UNINSREG "Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\$CompanyName $ProductName"
	
	; Get $ProductName file version for the Uninstall Registry key
	${GetFileVersion} "$INSTDIR\TStore.exe" $R0
	
	; Write the keys to the Registry
	WriteRegStr HKLM $UNINSREG "DisplayName" "$CompanyName $ProductName"
	WriteRegStr HKLM $UNINSREG "DisplayVersion" $R0
	WriteRegStr HKLM $UNINSREG "UninstallString" "$INSTDIR\uninstall.exe"
	WriteRegStr HKLM $UNINSREG "Publisher" "$CompanyName"
	
	; Write our Uninstaller
	WriteUninstaller "$INSTDIR\uninstall.exe"
SectionEnd

; This runs when the program is uninstalling
; Even with the Patch Installer, you MUST have the COMPLETE uninstall script (NSIS does not log actions like other tools such as Inno Setup or Windows Installer)
Section "Uninstall"
	; Switch Start Menu locations
	SetShellVarContext all
	
	; Grab the proper installation folder (in case the uninstaller is in the wrong place)
	ReadRegStr $INSTDIR HKLM "Software\$CompanyName\$ProductName" "Installation Folder"
	
	; Remove our Registry keys
	DetailPrint "Deleting Registry Keys"
	DeleteRegKey HKLM "Software\Microsoft Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\$CompanyName $ProductName"
	DeleteRegKey HKLM "Software\$CompanyName\$ProductName"
	DeleteRegKey /ifempty HKLM "Software\$CompanyName"
	
	; Remove $ProductName's executable
	DetailPrint "Uninstalling $ProductName"
	RMDir /r /REBOOTOK "$INSTDIR\Source"
	Delete "$INSTDIR\TStore.exe"
	Delete "$INSTDIR\TStore.exe.manifest"
	Delete "$INSTDIR\License.rtf"
	Delete "$INSTDIR\README.txt"
	Delete "$INSTDIR\TStore.ini"
	Delete "$INSTDIR\uninstall.exe"
	RMDir "$INSTDIR" ; DO NOT do a /r recursive search (in case, for example, someone installed to C:\Program Files this would really mess up the users computer)
	RMDir $PROGRAMFILES\$CompanyName ;AGAIN, do NOT use /r
	
	DetailPrint "Deleting Shortcuts"
	Delete "$SMPROGRAMS\$ProductName.lnk"
	
	; We are DONE with uninstall
	; As a reminder, DO NOT TOUCH any of the Microsoft DLLs that get installed
	; Also, $ProductName's per-user files do not get uninstalled (it's just not possible to remove files for users other than your own in the main uninstaller, however it is possible to release a utility that does PER-USER cleaning)
	
SectionEnd

; We need to do some checks when the installer and uninstaller are started.

; Tests for Admin rights NT4/2000/XP
; Also works if somehow UAC is disabled or broken on Vista+
; Also, on Windows NT 4.0, the Visual Basic runtime requires Service Pack 3 or later installed
Function .onInit
	; Company and Product
	StrCpy $CompanyName "RaggieSoft"
	StrCpy $ProductName "StoreTrainer"
	
	; Redefine the install folder (Setup will cross-check it later)
	StrCpy $INSTDIR "$PROGRAMFILES\$CompanyName\$ProductName"
	
	; Check for NT Admin Rights
	UserInfo::GetAccountType
	pop $0
	${If} $0 != "admin" ;Require admin rights on NT4+
		MessageBox MB_ICONSTOP|MB_OK "Administrator rights required to install $ProductName!" /SD IDOK
		SetErrorLevel 740 ;ERROR_ELEVATION_REQUIRED
		Quit
	${EndIf}

	; Check for NT 4.0 SP3 or higher
	; Otherwise, $ProductName *SHOULD* be able to run on any other 32bit or 64bit OS
	; That is Windows 95 or later.  Sorry Windows 3.1
	${If} ${IsNT}
		${If} ${IsWinNT4}
			${If} ${AtMostServicePack} 2
				MessageBox MB_ICONSTOP|MB_OK "Service Pack 3 or higher is required for Windows NT 4.0" /SD IDOK
				SetErrorLevel 3 ;3 because Service Pack 3 (pun intended)
				Quit
			${EndIf}
		${EndIf}
	${EndIf}
	
	; Since this is a Patch installer, check for a previous version of $ProductName
	ReadRegStr $PreviousInstallFolder HKLM "Software\$CompanyName\$ProductName" "Installation Folder"
	IfFileExists "$PreviousInstallFolder\TStore.exe" file_found file_not_found
	file_not_found:
		MessageBox mb_iconstop "This patch utility requires that you have $CompanyName $ProductName already installed!" /SD IDOK
		SetErrorLevel 7
		Quit
	file_found:
	${If} $PreviousInstallFolder == ""
		MessageBox mb_iconstop "This installer requires a previous version of $ProductName to be installed!" /SD IDOK
		SetErrorLevel 4
		Quit
	${Else}
		StrCpy $INSTDIR $PreviousInstallFolder
		${GetFileVersion} "$INSTDIR\TStore.exe" $TStoreVersionInstalled
		SetOutPath $TEMP
		File "..\Build\TStore.exe"
		${GetFileVersion} "$TEMP\TStore.exe" $TStoreVersionPatch
		${VersionCompare} "$TStoreVersionInstalled" "$TStoreVersionPatch" $TSVerCompare
		Delete "$TEMP\TStore.exe"
		
		${If} $TSVerCompare == 0
			MessageBox mb_iconstop "This patch is the same version of $ProductName you have!" /SD IDOK
			SetErrorLevel 5
			Quit
		${ElseIf} $TSVerCompare == 1
			MessageBox mb_iconstop "You have a newer version of $ProductName installed!" /SD IDOK
			SetErrorLevel 6
			Quit
		${EndIf}
	${EndIf}
FunctionEnd
Function un.onInit
	; Company and Product
	StrCpy $CompanyName "RaggieSoft"
	StrCpy $ProductName "StoreTrainer"
	UserInfo::GetAccountType
	pop $0
	${If} $0 != "admin" ;Require admin rights on NT4+
		MessageBox mb_iconstop "Administrator rights required to uninstall $ProductName!" /SD IDOK
		SetErrorLevel 740 ;ERROR_ELEVATION_REQUIRED
		Quit
	${EndIf}
FunctionEnd
